## Natural history notes

A palm-associated fungus characterized by small black, blister-like or cup-like fruiting bodies that erupt through the surface of palm leaves, often surrounded by yellowish spots or streaks. In Florida, it is found on living palm fronds in humid areas such as yards, parks, hammocks, swamps, gardens, and landscaped sites where susceptible palms are present. Rather than forming a mushroom, it grows as a leaf-spot fungus on palm foliage, producing dark spore-bearing structures that can make fronds look speckled or smutted, though infections are usually more cosmetic than lethal.
